context: Main eval: settings validation in Python where every ValueError message should follow the team convention (cannot <verb> <thing> "<value>": <expected or next step>) and the DATABASE_URL credentials must never reach a message.

checklist.name: Creates coherent settings.py artifact
checklist.description: Creates settings.py with load_settings(env) and a frozen Settings dataclass, using only the Python 3.12 standard library.

checklist.name: Preserves validation behavior
checklist.description: Returns Settings with parsed int port and workers, raises ValueError for a missing or invalid PORT, LOG_LEVEL, or DATABASE_URL and for an invalid WORKERS, checks in the listed order, and defaults WORKERS to 4.

checklist.name: Names the failed operation first
checklist.description: Every ValueError message starts with lowercase 'cannot', a verb, and the setting name, for example 'cannot read PORT'.

checklist.name: Quotes the offending value
checklist.description: Messages for an invalid PORT, LOG_LEVEL, or WORKERS value include the received value in double quotes right after the setting name. Missing-setting messages need no value.

checklist.name: States what was expected
checklist.description: Each message ends, after a colon, with the expected form or range (such as 'expected a whole number from 1 to 65535') or the step the operator can take.

checklist.name: Keeps the database password out of messages
checklist.description: No message, log call, or exception interpolates the DATABASE_URL value or any part of it that carries the user name or password. The DATABASE_URL message names the setting without echoing the URL.

checklist.name: Uses the plain one-line form
checklist.description: Messages have no 'Error:', 'Invalid', or 'Failed to' prefix, no apology, no exclamation mark, and no trailing period.

checklist.name: Keeps implementation focused
checklist.description: Adds no third-party dependencies, custom exception hierarchy, logging setup, or settings beyond the four requested.
